mainTopic: תמורה in special cases: the two kinds of substitution for מעשר בהמה, and רבי שמעון's view on an עולה bought with leftover money, ending the first פרק of תמורה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list of conditions for תמורה: the קרבן must not be one brought in partnership. רבי then explains why the תורה mentions תמורה separately for מעשר בהמה. מעשר has two kinds of substitution, תמורת שמו (a miscount that puts the 'tenth' name on the wrong animal) and תמורת גופו (a regular swap). He lists three ways they differ: being offered on the altar, being redeemed, and taking effect on a blemished animal. The גמרא explains that a separate mention was needed, because something taught with a new law has only that new law. Next, רבא explains that for רבי שמעון even a voluntary עולה makes a תמורה, and only an עולה bought with leftover money does not. The גמרא defends this, saying רבי שמעון agrees with רבי אליעזר that leftover money goes to a private offering but disagrees about תמורה. This raises a difficulty with רבי אבין's question about making a תמורה a second time. The גמרא answers that he asked about a תנא who combines both views, and the question ends unresolved (תיבעי). The amud closes the first פרק, הכל ממירין.

steps.title: The last condition: not an item brought in partnership
steps.stepSummary: The list of conditions for תמורה ends with one more requirement: the animal must be something that is not brought in partnership.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it must be an item that is not brought in partnership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list from the previous lines. תמורה only works on a קרבן that is not owned together by partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the list limited תמורה to certain kinds of קרבנות. This last line adds one more limit: a קרבן that comes from a partnership cannot make a תמורה. It closes that list, and next the גמרא moves to a new statement by רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitution: trying to swap a non-sacred animal for a קרבן. Both animals become holy.
Partnership: something owned or brought together by more than one person.

phrases.english: And an item that is not brought in partnership.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the list of conditions for תמורה from the previous lines of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תמורה takes effect only on a קרבן that is not brought in partnership.

steps.title: Why does the תורה mention substitution for the animal tithe separately?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks why מעשר בהמה is singled out for the law of תמורה, since the general law of תמורה was already stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: Why was the animal tithe singled out now?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks a question that sets up his next point. The general rule of תמורה already covers all קרבנות, so why does the תורה say it again about מעשר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a principle that when something is part of a general rule and the תורה mentions it separately, it is there to teach something new. רבי is asking what new thing the separate mention of מעשר comes to teach. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe: every tenth animal born in a year is holy and is brought as a קרבן.
Was taken out: singled out from a general rule to be mentioned on its own.
Now: here, after the general rule was already taught.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
Why was the tithe singled out now?
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק about מעשר that mentions swapping it, ויקרא 27:33.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה יָצָא מַעֲשֵׂר מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how תמורה works for מעשר in particular.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the purpose of the תורה's separate mention of תמורה for מעשר בהמה?

steps.title: Answer: to teach about two kinds of substitution
steps.stepSummary: מעשר is mentioned separately in order to discuss both תמורת שמו and תמורת גופו.
steps.simpleTranslation: To discuss 'substitution of its name' and 'substitution of its body.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers his own question. מעשר has a special kind of 'switch' that other קרבנות don't have, so the תורה needed to talk about it separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמורת שמו happens when the counter mistakenly calls the eleventh animal 'tenth'. The name of מעשר moves onto the wrong animal, and that animal becomes holy too. תמורת גופו is the regular swap that applies to all קרבנות. Since מעשר has this unusual name-switch, the תורה makes clear that the regular swap also applies to it, and the two kinds have different rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitution of its name: a miscount where the 'tenth' label lands on the wrong animal.
Substitution of its body: a regular swap, 'this animal instead of that one.'
To be discussed (judged): to be treated with its own special rules.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds. תמורת שמו is a counting mistake about which animal is the tenth. תמורת גופו is a deliberate swap of an animal for one that is already מעשר.

phrases.english: To be discussed regarding 'substitution of its name'
phrases.notes: This is when the counter calls the ninth or eleventh animal 'tenth' by mistake.

phrases.english: and 'substitution of its body.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לִידּוֹן בִּתְמוּרַת שְׁמוֹ וּבִתְמוּרַת גּוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The separate mention of מעשר teaches that it has two kinds of substitution, תמורת שמו and תמורת גופו, and that each has its own rules.

steps.title: Two differences: offering on the altar and redemption
steps.stepSummary: תמורת שמו is offered on the altar and can be redeemed. תמורת גופו is not offered and cannot be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is to tell you: a substitute of its name is offered, but a substitute of its body is not offered. A substitute of its name is redeemed, but a substitute of its body is not redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי now spells out how the two kinds of substitution are different. He gives two differences here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal that got the 'tenth' name by mistake becomes like a שלמים. That is why it is brought on the altar, and if it gets a blemish it can be redeemed. An animal swapped for מעשר is holy but is not brought on the altar, and the פסוק says about מעשר 'it shall not be redeemed' (ויקרא 27:33). With other קרבנות, the swapped animal has the same status as the original. Here, with מעשר, the swapped animal gets a different and stricter result.

keyTerms.meaning: Is offered on the altar.
Is redeemed: it can be exchanged for money, and the holiness moves onto the money.

phrases.english: To tell you: a substitute of its name is offered,
a substitute of its body is not offered;
a substitute of its name is redeemed,
phrases.notes: This means once it gets a blemish, just like a regular שלמים.

phrases.english: a substitute of its body is not redeemed.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the practical rules for the two kinds of substitution named in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תמורת שמו of מעשר is brought on the altar and can be redeemed. תמורת גופו is neither brought on the altar nor redeemed.

steps.title: Third difference: fit and unfit animals
steps.stepSummary: תמורת גופו takes effect even on a blemished animal. תמורת שמו takes effect only on an animal that is fit for the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: A substitute of its body takes effect on a fit item and on an unfit item. But a substitute of its name takes effect only on a fit item.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives one more difference: which animals each kind of substitution can make holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular swap with מעשר works even on a blemished animal, because the holiness of מעשר can rest even on a blemished animal. The name-switch makes the animal like a שלמים that gets brought on the altar, so it only works if the animal is fit. If the animal wrongly called 'tenth' is blemished, it does not become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: A fit item: an animal with no blemish that can be brought on the altar.
Takes effect: the holiness actually rests on the animal.
Only.

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר has two kinds of substitution. תמורת שמו (the miscount) is brought on the altar, can be redeemed, and works only on a fit animal. תמורת גופו (the regular swap) is not brought on the altar, cannot be redeemed, and works even on a blemished animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'name' of מעשר is a real source of holiness, but a different one from a regular swap. Each one follows its own logic.

phrases.aramaic: תְּמוּרַת גּוּפוֹ — חָלָה עַל דָּבָר הָרָאוּי
phrases.english: A substitute of its body takes effect on a fit item
and on an item that is not fit,
but a substitute of its name does not take effect
except on a fit item only.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּמוּרַת גּוּפוֹ חָלָה עַל דָּבָר הָרָאוּי וְעַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third difference to the two given in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תמורת גופו of מעשר takes effect on fit and unfit animals alike. תמורת שמו takes effect only on a fit animal.

steps.title: Would a special extra law take away the regular law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבי's answer: just because the תורה added תמורת שמו for מעשר, why would we think מעשר loses regular תמורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Just because the תורה gave מעשר the extra law of תמורת שמו, does that mean it loses something?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 3. Why would an added law make us think the normal law of תמורה stops applying to מעשר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 said מעשר is mentioned separately so the תורה could teach both תמורת שמו and תמורת גופו. That only makes sense if we might have thought מעשר has no תמורת גופו. The challenge: getting an extra law should only add to מעשר, not take something away.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Substitution of its name: calling a different animal by the מעשר's name
Is it really made weaker? Does it lose something?

phrases.english: They say: Because the Merciful One included
that it has substitution of its name,
phrases.notes: "It" is מעשר בהמה, the animal tithe.

phrases.english: is it then diminished?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי רַחֲמָנָא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ תְּמוּרַת שְׁמוֹ, אִיגְּרוֹעֵי אִיגְּרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 3 for mentioning מעשר separately
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a separate verse was needed to teach תמורת גופו for מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An extra law only adds. It should not make us think the regular law of תמורה is removed, so no separate verse should be needed.

steps.title: Yes: the תורה's inclusion covers only what it says
steps.stepSummary: Yes, we could have thought so, because what the תורה included is included, and what it did not include is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. As we say: what the תורה included is included, and what it did not include is not included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Yes, without a separate verse we really would have said מעשר has only תמורת שמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה talks about מעשר's תמורה in terms of its name. So we would limit מעשר to exactly what was said there and nothing more. That is why a separate mention was needed to add תמורת גופו too.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Included (from the root רבה, to add or include)
What it included, it included: we go only by exactly what the verse said

phrases.english: Yes, for we say:
what it included, it included,
and what it did not include, it did not include.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דְּאָמְרִינַן: מַאי דְּרַבִּי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise of the question and defends it with a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An extra law could only add to מעשר, so no separate verse was needed
steps.terutzMaskana: Without a verse we would limit מעשר to תמורת שמו alone, so the separate mention is needed

steps.title: Where does that limiting rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the idea that מעשר gets only what was specifically stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where would this idea come from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind Step 7's rule. This sets up the answer of רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we do not assume a special law cancels the general law. So the גמרא wants to know why מעשר should be limited here.

keyTerms.meaning: And this (idea)
From where
Would it come; would we know it

phrases.english: And from where would this come?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מֵהֵיכָא תֵּיתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the rule stated in Step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason we would limit מעשר to only what was said about it

steps.title: Something taught as a new law has only that new law
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains that the case of מעשר is a דבר הבא לידון בדבר החדש, so it has only its new law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: Because it is something that comes to be taught with a new law, and it has only its new law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives the source. When the תורה teaches something a brand-new law, we limit it to that new law alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמורת שמו is a new law that exists only for מעשר. Since the תורה handled מעשר with a new law, we would not apply other laws to it, such as regular תמורת גופו. That is why a separate mention was needed to include it.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter that comes to be judged with a new law
Its new law, its novelty
Only

steps.whatToRemember: A case the תורה teaches with a new law gets only that new law. That is why a separate mention was needed to give מעשר regular תמורה as well.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Because it is a matter that comes
to be judged with a new matter,
phrases.notes: The "new matter" here is תמורת שמו, which only מעשר has.

phrases.english: and it has only its novelty alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה דָּבָר הַבָּא לִידּוֹן בְּדָבָר הֶחָדָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule of דבר הבא לידון בדבר החדש: a case taught with a new law is limited to that new law

steps.title: For רבי שמעון, does a voluntary עולה not make a תמורה?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא: if רבי שמעון says only an obligatory offering makes a תמורה, does a voluntary עולה not make one?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: According to רבי שמעון, who said only something that comes as an obligation, is it only an obligatory עולה that makes a תמורה, but not a voluntary עולה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא how far רבי שמעון's rule goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון limits תמורה to an offering brought as an obligation (חובה). Read simply, that seems to leave out every voluntary offering, even a regular voluntary עולה. רב נחמן בר יצחק asks whether that is really so.

keyTerms.meaning: Something brought as an obligation
An עולה one is required to bring
A voluntary עולה, a free-will offering
Substitution: switching a consecrated animal for another, which makes the second animal holy too

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said to Rava:
According to Rabbi Shimon, who said
"a matter that comes as an obligation"
is it an obligatory burnt offering that makes a substitute,
but a voluntary burnt offering does not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר דָּבָר הַבָּא בְּחוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about רבי שמעון's rule of דבר הבא בחובה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a voluntary עולה makes a תמורה according to רבי שמעון

steps.title: A voluntary עולה also counts once it is taken on
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a voluntary עולה also makes a תמורה, since once a person takes it on, it is an obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A voluntary עולה also. Since he took it upon himself, it makes a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that a voluntary עולה is included in רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדבה starts out as a choice. But once someone vows to bring it, he must bring it. So it becomes a חובה and fits רבי שמעון's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Also
Since he took it upon himself
It makes a substitute

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think "voluntary" means "not an obligation" here. Once a person commits to a נדבה, it becomes his obligation.

phrases.english: He said to him: A voluntary burnt offering also,
since he accepted it upon himself,
it makes a substitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עוֹלַת נְדָבָה נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּקַבְּלַהּ עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A voluntary עולה counts as a חובה once the person takes it on, so it makes a תמורה

steps.title: The rule only leaves out an עולה from leftover money
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי שמעון's rule only comes to exclude an עולה bought with leftover money.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed only for an עולה that comes from leftover money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer. He tells us which עולה רבי שמעון's rule actually leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a voluntary עולה counts as a חובה, we might ask what רבי שמעון's rule leaves out at all. רבא answers: an עולה bought with money left over from another offering. Nobody ever took that עולה on himself, so it does not make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for
Leftover money from funds set aside for another offering
Burnt offering

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, both an obligatory עולה and a voluntary one make a תמורה. Only an עולה bought with leftover money does not.

phrases.english: And it was needed only
for a burnt offering that comes from the surplus.
phrases.notes: He means: רבי שמעון's rule only comes to leave out this kind of עולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא נִצְרְכָה, אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָה הַבָּאָה מִן הַמּוֹתָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's answer by saying what the חובה rule leaves out
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון's rule of דבר הבא בחובה leaves out only an עולה bought with leftover money. Obligatory and voluntary עולות both make a תמורה.

steps.title: If leftover money goes to communal offerings, the rule is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון holds about leftover money. If he holds it goes to communal offerings, his rule is pointless, since communal offerings never make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does רבי שמעון hold? If he holds like the view that leftover money goes to communal gift offerings, then it is obvious that this עולה does not make a תמורה, because communal offerings never make a תמורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבא's explanation from Step 12. It asks which view about leftover money רבי שמעון holds, and shows that the first option makes his rule pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument about where leftover money (מותרות) goes: to communal offerings, or to a private gift offering. If רבי שמעון holds it goes to communal offerings, then an עולה from that money is a communal offering. We already know communal offerings never make a תמורה, so he would not need to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover money, set aside for an offering but not all used
A communal gift offering, paid for by the whole community
Swapping a regular animal for a holy one. Both animals become holy
It is obvious, so why would anyone need to say it?
Communal offerings cannot make a תמורה

phrases.english: What does he hold?
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי שמעון. The question is where he holds leftover money goes.

phrases.english: If he holds like the one who said
leftover funds go to communal gift offerings
it is obvious that it does not make a תמורה,
since there is no תמורה with a communal offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר לַהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's explanation from Step 12 by checking which view about leftover money רבי שמעון holds.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי שמעון's rule comes to exclude an עולה bought with leftover money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If leftover money goes to communal offerings, the עולה is communal. Communal offerings never make a תמורה anyway, so the rule would teach nothing new.

steps.title: Maybe רבי שמעון holds leftover money goes to a private offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the other option: רבי שמעון holds that leftover money goes to a private gift offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי שמעון holds like the view that leftover money goes to an individual's gift offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option to save רבא's explanation. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the leftover money buys a private עולה, then it is not a communal offering. Now רבי שמעון's rule that it does not make a תמורה is no longer obvious, so it teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Drops one option and tries another
A private gift offering, brought by one person
They go (to), meaning the money is used for

phrases.english: Rather, רבי שמעון holds
like the one who said
leftover funds go to an individual's gift offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the communal option from Step 13 and suggests the private option instead.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks a different background view for רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון might hold that leftover money goes to communal offerings
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון holds that leftover money goes to a private offering, so his rule teaches something new

steps.title: But רבי אליעזר holds that view and says it does make a תמורה
steps.stepSummary: The view that leftover money goes to a private offering belongs to רבי אליעזר. A ברייתא says clearly that he holds such an עולה does make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom do we know holds this reasoning? רבי אליעזר! But we heard him say clearly that it does make a תמורה, as a ברייתא teaches: "An עולה that comes from leftover money makes a תמורה." These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion from Step 14. The only one known to say leftover money goes to a private offering is רבי אליעזר, and he rules the opposite of what רבא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 put רבי שמעון in רבי אליעזר's camp. But רבי אליעזר says outright that an עולה from leftover money does make a תמורה. So how could רבי שמעון's rule exclude it?

keyTerms.meaning: A line of reasoning or a view
Clearly, in so many words
An עולה bought with leftover money

phrases.english: Whom have you heard holds this reasoning?
רבי אליעזר!
But we have heard him say clearly
that it does make a תמורה,
as a ברייתא teaches: "An עולה that comes from leftover funds
makes a תמורה",
these are the words of רבי אליעזר!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ הַאי סְבָרָא? רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of Step 14 by pointing to the view's known owner, רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי שמעון holds leftover money goes to a private offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That view belongs to רבי אליעזר, who says clearly in a ברייתא that such an עולה does make a תמורה. This is the opposite of what רבא said in רבי שמעון's name.

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees with רבי אליעזר on one point and argues on the other
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון agrees that leftover money goes to a private עולה. He disagrees about תמורה and holds that such an עולה does not make one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון agrees with him on one point and argues with him on another. רבי אליעזר holds that an עולה from leftover money makes a תמורה, and רבי שמעון holds it does not make a תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי שמעון does not have to follow רבי אליעזר on everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate questions: where the leftover money goes, and whether that עולה makes a תמורה. רבי שמעון agrees with רבי אליעזר on the first, so it is a private עולה. He disagrees on the second, so it does not make a תמורה. This keeps רבא's explanation standing.

keyTerms.meaning: He agrees with him on one point
He argues with him
It makes a תמורה, so a swapped animal becomes holy

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, an עולה bought with leftover money is a private offering, but it does not make a תמורה. רבי אליעזר holds that it does.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two questions. Agreeing about where the money goes does not mean agreeing about תמורה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: רבי שמעון agrees with him on one point,
and argues with him on one point,
for רבי אליעזר holds:
an עולה that comes from leftover funds
makes a תמורה,
and he holds: it does not make a תמורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 by separating the two points of disagreement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the issue: agrees on one point, argues on the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי שמעון holds like רבי אליעזר about leftover money, he must also agree about תמורה
steps.terutzMaskana: He agrees that the money goes to a private עולה but holds that this עולה does not make a תמורה

steps.title: A new challenge from רבי אבין's question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a challenge: if so, why did רבי אבין ask whether an אשם that was switched to an עולה can make a תמורה again?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, consider what רבי אבין asked: someone set aside an אשם to gain atonement with it, and he made a תמורה with it. Then he gained atonement with a different אשם, and this one was switched to be an עולה. Can he make a תמורה with it again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new challenge to the answer of Step 16 by bringing in a question from רבי אבין. The next step finishes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין's case is an animal that became an עולה because it was left over and no longer needed, so it is like an עולה from leftovers. If רבי שמעון holds clearly that such an עולה does not make a תמורה, it is hard to see why רבי אבין would ask.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. Introduces a problem with what was just said
He asked, raising an open question
A guilt offering, brought for certain sins
He made a תמורה (swapped an animal)
It was switched to be brought as an עולה
What is the law?

phrases.english: If so,
then what about the question רבי אבין asked:
he set aside an אשם to gain atonement with it,
and he made a תמורה with it,
and he gained atonement with a different אשם,
and this one was switched to be an עולה
phrases.notes: The first אשם is no longer needed, so it is moved over to be brought as an עולה.

phrases.english: can he make a תמורה with it again?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, דְּבָעֵי רַבִּי אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge to the answer of Step 16 by bringing רבי אבין's question about an אשם switched to an עולה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that, according to רבי שמעון, an עולה from leftovers does not make a תמורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule were that clear, רבי אבין would have no reason to ask whether a leftover אשם that became an עולה can make a תמורה. Step 18 completes the challenge.

steps.title: Whose view could רבי אבין's question follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. רבי אבין's question can't follow רבי שמעון, because רבי שמעון holds that an עולה from leftover money makes no תמורה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this question based on? If you say it follows רבי שמעון, you just said that רבי שמעון holds an עולה that comes from leftover money does not make a תמורה at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the challenge it started in step 17. It asks which תנא רבי אבין's question could fit, and shows it can't be רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבין asks whether a תמורה can be made a second time. That question only arises for someone who holds you cannot make a תמורה twice, and that is רבי שמעון's view, so the question seems to follow him. It also assumes this leftover עולה can make a תמורה at all. But in step 16 we said רבי שמעון holds it makes no תמורה, so for him there is nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whose opinion?
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Leftover money set aside for a קרבן that ended up not being needed
An animal someone tried to swap for a holy animal; it becomes holy too

phrases.english: According to whom?
phrases.notes: He means: whose opinion was רבי אבין's question built on?

phrases.english: If you say it is according to רבי שמעון —

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: but you said that רבי שמעון holds:
a burnt offering that comes from leftover money
does not make a substitute!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן? אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge that step 17 began
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 16 that רבי שמעון holds an עולה from leftover money makes no תמורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question about a second תמורה assumes the view that one cannot make a תמורה twice, which is רבי שמעון's view. But רבי שמעון holds that an עולה from leftover money makes no תמורה at all, so for him the question has nothing to ask about.

steps.title: רבי אבין asked about a תנא who mixes two views
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין's question is about a תנא who agrees with רבי שמעון that you can't make a תמורה twice, and with רבי אליעזר that an עולה from leftover money does make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי אבין was asking: Suppose you find a תנא who holds like רבי שמעון, who says you cannot make a תמורה and then make another one. Suppose he also holds like רבי אליעזר, who says an עולה from leftover money does make a תמורה. Can this person make a תמורה again with this animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי אבין was not following רבי שמעון alone. He was asking about a תנא who takes one rule from רבי שמעון and another from רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question needs two rules at once. The first rule is that a תמורה can't be made twice, which comes from רבי שמעון. The second is that an עולה from leftover money can make a תמורה, which comes from רבי אליעזר. Only a תנא who holds both has a real question about whether this עולה counts as a new start.

keyTerms.meaning: He was asking (his question was)
A sage of the משנה period
You cannot make a תמורה and then make another one from the same holy animal
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אבין is asking according to רבי שמעון himself. He is asking according to an imagined תנא who combines רבי שמעון's rule with רבי אליעזר's rule.

phrases.english: This is what רבי אבין was asking:

phrases.aramaic: אִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ תַּנָּא דְּקָאֵי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: If you find a תנא who stands with רבי שמעון,
who says one cannot make a substitute and then make a substitute again,
and he also holds like רבי אליעזר,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר עוֹלָה הַבָּאָה מִן הַמּוֹתָרוֹת עוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה,
phrases.english: who says a burnt offering from leftover money does make a substitute,
what is the law: can he go back and make a substitute with it again?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אָבִין הָכִי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining whose view the question follows: a תנא who holds both views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבין's question was based on רבי שמעון alone, so it made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question fits a תנא who holds like רבי שמעון on making a תמורה twice and like רבי אליעזר on leftover money.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a question in the גמרא can be built on a mix of opinions. That keeps רבי אבין's question meaningful.

steps.title: First case: two animals with one holiness
steps.stepSummary: The first part of רבי אבין's question: what if there are two different animals but both have the same type of holiness?
steps.simpleTranslation: With two bodies and one holiness, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the first part of רבי אבין's question. Now it is asked within the view of the combined תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a new animal took over the same holiness as the first one, and the first one had already made a תמורה. Does the new body allow a new תמורה, or does the same holiness block it? The second part of the question comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Bodies, meaning separate animals
One holiness, the same type of קרבן status
What is the law?

phrases.english: With two bodies and one holiness, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Two separate animals, but both carry the same holiness, like a replacement animal for the first one.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁנֵי גוּפִין וּקְדוּשָּׁה אַחַת, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first part of the question set up in step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a תמורה be made again when the animal is new but the holiness is the same?

steps.title: Second case: one animal with two holinesses, left unanswered
steps.stepSummary: Even if two animals with one holiness can't make a new תמורה, what about one animal that got a second, different holiness? The question stays open: תיבעי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that when it's one holiness he can't, what about two holinesses and one body? The question stays unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the second part of רבי אבין's question and ends with תיבעי. This means no answer was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the first case was blocked only because the holiness stayed the same. Here the same animal moves to a new holiness, like an אשם that later becomes an עולה, so it might count as a fresh start. For the combined תנא, the גמרא leaves this unresolved.

keyTerms.meaning: If you end up saying (if the first question is answered this way)
Two holinesses, two different קרבן statuses
One body, the same animal
Let it stand as a question; it stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבין's question only makes sense for a תנא who holds like רבי שמעון (no second תמורה) and like רבי אליעזר (an עולה from leftovers makes a תמורה). For that תנא, the question of one animal with two holinesses stays open: תיבעי.

phrases.english: And if you say:
with one holiness, he cannot,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Either way, read it as: when the holiness is the same, he can't make another תמורה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת וְגוּף אֶחָד, מַאי?
phrases.english: but with two holinesses and one body, what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּימְצָא לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the first case in step 20 and adds the second case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can a תמורה be made again when the animal stays the same but its holiness changes?

steps.title: Hadran — Closing הכל ממירין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally finishes the first פרק of מסכת תמורה, הכל ממירין, with the traditional closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הכל ממירין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not a new argument. It is the traditional line said when a פרק of גמרא is finished, and here it closes the first פרק of תמורה, הכל ממירין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last discussion ended with רבי אבין's question left open as a תיבעי, so no answer was given. The Hadran simply marks that the learning of this פרק is complete. The words 'we will return to you' show a promise to come back and review it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the closing line said when a פרק is finished
All may make a תמורה; the name of the first פרק of תמורה, taken from its opening words

steps.whatToRemember: The first פרק of תמורה, הכל ממירין, is now complete. Its last סוגיא ended with רבי אבין's question about making a תמורה a second time left open as a תיבעי.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read הכל ממירין here as a new ruling that everyone can make a תמורה. In this line it is just the name of the פרק being closed.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
"All may make a substitute."

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ הַכֹּל מְמִירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי אבין's question is left open as a תיבעי in step 21, the פרק formally ends.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first פרק of תמורה, הכל ממירין, is complete.
